newsitem.title: USA: USDA--4 detections in national Karnal bunt survey.
newsitem.headline: USDA--4 detections in national Karnal bunt survey.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday there were four confirmed detections of Tilletia indica spores, the smut fungus that causes Karnal bunt, outside the quarantine area in elevator surveys.
But USDA emphasized the detection of spores does not necessarily mean the disease is present, and more testing is required.
USDA is in the midst of a nationwide Karnal bunt survey prompted by the discovery of the durum wheat fungus last Spring in parts of Southwest, which led to a quarantine.

The first detection was in California and subsequent tests on 400 other samples all proved negative. The other detections were on wheat from Alabama, USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) said in a Karnal bunt update.
USDA is conducting additional tests after one positive detection in Baldwin County, Alabama.
More recently, two composites of wheat from two different Alabama counties sampled at elevators in Alabama and Florida tested positive by DNA testing for Tilletia indica spores.
USDA said emergency action notifications are being placed on both elevators and the disposition of the grain will be determined. It said further investigations are proceeding.

"As a precaution, surveillance efforts will continue to be intensified in all four areas where positive spores were detected," the APHIS update said. "At this time, the detected spores of Tilletia indica do not indicate Karnal bunt is established in the field in California, Alabama or Florida."
USDA also said a positive spore detection was confirmed at a storage facility within the regulated area in Luna County, N.M., and that routine procedures were followed.
